components.name: Dot Field
components.description: A liquid field of grey (Ink) dashes on a fixed canvas across the whole page, Antigravity-style. Poisson-disc particles (26px), faded to a faint 14% under the text column and within 16px of it, brightening over 110px. A ring (30% of the larger screen side) trails the mouse with a 0.45s ease and circles a resting mouse; with no mouse it wanders widely. It breathes and is noise-edged. Particles on its band swell into dashes that point away from the centre; inside are medium dashes and outside are specks. Sizes ease over 0.22s, and gradient noise keeps everything drifting. Mouse only; one still frame under reduced motion. Decorative and aria-hidden.
components.css: .ds-field { position: relative; width: 100%; height: 10rem; overflow: hidden; pointer-events: none; } .ds-field span { position: absolute; height: 2px; border-radius: 1px; background: var(--color-ink); }

narrative.overview:
One narrow column on a cool near-white with a faint blue cast, about 640px, read top to bottom like a well-made personal page. It runs name, short bio, availability, three links (Email, GitHub, LinkedIn), a sliding strip of technology logos, the chip, four project cards, experience, six more repos with a link to the rest on GitHub, and how to reach them. Instrument Serif at 400 carries the voice moments: the 40px name, card titles and dialog titles. Instrument Sans carries everything else at small, even sizes. JetBrains Mono appears only where the content is literally code, a file name or a chip marking.

The owner's standing steer governs every surface: "not too bold, professionalism with taste". The page stays a summary. Each featured project is a soft blue-gray card (14px radius) with a serif title, year, one short summary, tags and "View project". The card opens a native dialog keyed to the URL hash, and the full story lives there. That story is the overview, a live diagram of the project working, gesture data or a code listing, a Details list and the source link. Whitespace groups the page. Hairlines appear only in lists: More projects, the dialog's Details, the dialog foot and the footer.

The DIP-8 chip figure is the only signature and the only place the old datasheet idea survives. Light only, by design (`color-scheme: light`).
keyCharacteristics: Cool near-white page with a faint blue cast, near-black ink, two quieter greys, blue-gray hairlines.
Visuals and project cards sit in soft Panel fills with a 14px radius. The dialog is the one Paper surface lifted off the page.
Serif for names and titles, sans for everything else, mono only for literal code and markings.
Links are ink with a light blue-gray underline that darkens on hover. Blue is not a link colour.
Blue, the only accent, marks focus, the active pin, the gesture skeletons and one status word.
One shadow in the system, on the open dialog.
Motion is a 160ms colour change, plus a 200ms dialog rise and a pausable 45s tech strip. Both of those stop under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Slate On Paper Rule
rules.body: Slate (`ink-3`) sits on Paper only. It clears AA on Paper (4.97:1) but only just clears it on Panel (4.57:1) and falls below it on a hovered card (4.25:1). Text inside a panel or card uses Graphite (5.19:1 on Panel, 4.82:1 on a hovered card) or Ink, which is why card meta and tags are Graphite.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue is the only accent. It marks focus, the active pin, the gesture bones and the "In development" status word (5.22:1 on Panel, 4.85:1 on a hovered card). It is never decoration, a heading colour, a link colour or a fill.

rules.name: The Serif Names Rule
rules.body: Instrument Serif sets names only: the person, a card title and a dialog title. It is always weight 400, and only the serif goes above 1rem. Sans text stays between 0.75rem and 1rem, and its emphasis comes from weight (500 for links, labels and list names) and from moving between Ink, Graphite and Slate.

rules.name: The Literal Mono Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is for text that is literally code, a file name, a gesture name, a pin name or a chip marking (numerals, date code, readout key). It is always weight 400 and never used for prose, labels or headings. The KDC-14 mark is sans, not mono.

rules.name: The Space Groups Rule
rules.body: Group with whitespace and the panel fill. Hairlines are for lists only: More projects rows, the Details facts, the rule above the dialog foot and the footer. Never put dividers between sections or between cards.

rules.name: The Summary And Story Rule
rules.body: The page carries a summary of each project. The full story (media, overview, live diagram, figures, facts and source) lives in that project's dialog, reachable by URL hash.

rules.name: The One Lift Rule
rules.body: The modal dialog is the only element with a shadow and a backdrop. Cards, panels, the chip and buttons stay flat. Hover changes tone, never elevation.

dos: Do present each featured project as a Panel card (14px radius, 1rem grid gap, two up from 40rem) that opens its full story in a hash-keyed dialog.
Do keep the open dialog the only lifted surface: Paper, 18px radius, one soft shadow, 40% ink backdrop, a bottom sheet below 40rem.
Do make links Ink with a Hairline Strong underline that darkens on hover over 160ms.
Do separate sections and cards with space (5rem to 6.5rem between sections), and keep hairlines for lists.
Do set names in Instrument Serif 400, code, file names and pin names in JetBrains Mono 400, and everything else in Instrument Sans.
Do keep Slate text on Paper and use Graphite or Ink inside panels and cards.
Do keep motion to 160ms colour changes, the 200ms dialog rise and the pausable tech strip, and turn the rise and the strip off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
donts: Don't add a header bar, navigation, numbered sections or tables.
Don't box tags or turn them into pills; tags are plain text joined by middle dots. The dialog's Close button is the only pill.
Don't use blue for links or decoration, or add a second accent colour.
Don't put a shadow on anything but the open dialog, and don't lift cards on hover.
Don't add a dark mode; the system is light only by design.
Don't put a label, kicker or eyebrow above the name, a section title, a card title or a dialog title.
Don't set sans text larger than 1rem or use the serif for anything but names.
Don't add a second signature figure or extend the chip's hardware styling to other components.
Don't add page-load or scroll-triggered entrance animations, or autoplaying media.
